candidates.action: approaches jump, changes body/skis orientation in the air
candidates.after: airborne body is visibly tilted; landing is outside this candidate
candidates.camera: following third-person camera; screen center alone cannot measure world orientation
candidates.occlusion: body silhouette generally separable; other riders and motion blur require interval-level exclusion
candidates.ui: score/controls near edges; bottom captions require clearance
candidates.reason: approach and ensuing body change are easier to connect than a clip starting midway through a trick
candidates.nextReview: extend through18seconds and track body landmarks before selecting a final teaching cut

candidates.action: body tilts then returns to skiing and banking
candidates.after: continues forward with changing ski/body alignment
candidates.occlusion: rider fairly clear, other rider nearby
candidates.reason: useful to compare orientation changes; weaker first introduction because jump approach is missing

candidates.occlusion: large rock/tree hides or competes with the body in the middle
candidates.reason: obstruction interrupts the direction line; a first-time viewer must spend effort finding the body

candidates.before: bike and rider lean on snow trail
candidates.action: moves alongside another rider and banks through trees
candidates.camera: camera banks/moves with rider; cannot equate screen tilt with a world-axis angle
candidates.occlusion: nearby rider and tree trunks compete with wheel/body visibility
candidates.reason: can motivate inverse rotation with qualified screen-space landmarks after axes are explained; less clear than A for initial position/orientation distinction

annotationPolicy.red: observed torso/body direction on projected screen
annotationPolicy.teal: clearly labelled screen reference or retained earlier direction
